key_insight: A quantum-assisted agentic framework turns each microgrid control step into a QUBO and uses deadline-aware solver selection to achieve exact, real-time dispatch optimization.
engineering_relevance: This enables hybrid renewable microgrids to coordinate batteries, generation, and demand response under hard control deadlines while reducing operating cost and preserving high renewable utilization.
method: BDIx agents formulate per-slot dispatch and coalition decisions as QUBO problems.
A coordinator agent selects among quantum, quantum-inspired, and classical solvers based on learned latency beliefs and the current deadline.
A storage valuation mechanism prices battery energy using discounted future-peak value to add intertemporal awareness.
evidence_signal: In a 24-hour microgrid simulation, the framework missed zero deadlines, matched the exact optimum in every slot, achieved a daily cost of 146.24 EUR, and reached 97.83% renewable utilization with no unserved energy.
watch_item: The reported QAOA results rely on statevector simulation, so practical performance on real quantum hardware and larger-scale grids may differ.
paper_title: A Quantum-Assisted Agentic Distributed Artificial Intelligence Framework for Deadline-Bounded Orchestration of Hybrid Renewable Microgrids
